## PART 1 – Question 1

Read the notice and decide whether each statement is TRUE or FALSE.

> **SCHOOL ENTRANCE AHEAD**  
> **DEAD SLOW**

statements.content: Parents must stay away from the gate.
The sign is meant for drivers.
There is a school gate near the sign.
Schoolchildren have to walk slowly.

questions.explanation: The notice warns drivers that a school entrance is ahead and asks them to drive very slowly.

questions.content:
## Question 2

Read the advertisement.

> **GRAY & SONS**  
> **BUILDERS**  
> Since 1983  
> Free estimates

statements.content: Gray and Sons builds houses.
Gray and Sons estimates the size of your house for free.
Gray and Sons gives builders houses for free.
Gray and Sons has been in the business since 1983.

questions.explanation: Free estimates means customers can receive a free estimate of the expected cost; it does not mean free houses or size measurement.

## Question 7

Read the message.

> **From:** Joy  
> **To:** Linh  
> Hi Linh. I’ll be in town on business this Friday, so how about meeting for dinner then, instead of Tuesday as usual?  
> Joy

statements.content: Joy wants Linh to meet her on Tuesday this week.
The message is meant for Linh.
Joy and Linh often meet for dinner on Friday.
Joy is with Linh on a business trip to town.

questions.explanation: Joy writes to Linh and proposes Friday instead of their usual Tuesday meeting. Joy, not both of them, will be in town on business.

questions.content:
## PART 2 – Question 8

Fifty-two-year-old American Henry Evans is one of the world's first teletourists. From the comfort of his bed in Palo Alto, California, he has travelled to places as far away as Bora Bora in the South Pacific. Under normal circumstances, this journey would be impossible for Henry because he is disabled. A serious stroke when he was 40 affected his brain and left him without speech and unable to use his arms or legs. But with the help of technology, Henry is able to deal with his difficulties and get out to see the world.

Decide whether each statement is TRUE or FALSE.

statements.content: Henry suffers from severe and lasting post-stroke disability.
Henry has been disabled since he was born.
Henry has only visited domestic destinations virtually so far.
It is impossible for Henry to travel physically to faraway places.

questions.explanation: Henry became disabled after a stroke at 40, has virtually visited distant international destinations, and cannot normally make those physical journeys.

questions.content:
## Question 9

When Henry wants to visit a museum, he uses a telepresence robot called the Beam, a big computer monitor with a webcam that is attached to a mobile base with two poles. Using head movements, he can drive the machine around the halls, talking to the guide and learning about the exhibits, just like any other visitor. Several of the world's museums already use these machines, and Henry hopes there will soon be more.

Decide whether each statement is TRUE or FALSE.

statements.content: Henry can visit museums with the help of a telepresence robot.
Robots like the Beam are being used widely in museums across the world.
Henry uses sign language to communicate directly with museum guides.
The Beam is attached permanently to museums’ walls.

questions.explanation: Only several museums currently use the mobile Beam robot. Henry controls it with head movements and talks through it.

questions.content:
## Questions 10–15

To see what is happening outside, Henry uses a device called Polly. Like the Beam, Polly is made up of a monitor and a webcam, the difference being that it is small enough to be portable. The gadget fits into a frame attached to a person's shoulder allowing it to be carried around like a parrot. By virtue of this new technology, Henry can accompany and converse with his friends and family when they have a day out in the country. He controls it by moving his head, so that it turns around and shows him everything his companions can see and hear.

Thanks to improvements in long-distance remote-control software, Henry can fly drones, which also enable him to explore from the air. When he wants to go further afield, he has found a website which has 5,000 drone videos from all over the world, which gives him access to all kinds of fascinating destinations.

No journey is too far for Henry, who is currently pursuing the possibility of travelling into space. He got the idea from an article he came across on the internet. He read that a research team was trying to get access for PC users to a robot on the International Space Station (ISS). Henry has already applied for permission to use this new technology, but he has not received approval yet. Judging by what he has already achieved, however, it is only a matter of time before he is allowed to go on a remote tour of the satellite.

questions.question: In paragraph 3, the phrase “made up” is closest in meaning to ____.
questions.explanation: Made up of means formed or composed of.

questions.question: In paragraph 3, the word “it” refers to ____.
questions.explanation: Polly is small enough to be portable.

questions.question: How does Polly differ from Beam according to paragraph 3?
questions.option_a: Polly is made up of completely different components from the Beam.
questions.option_b: Polly is considerably smaller in size than the Beam.
questions.option_c: Polly can’t be controlled by head movements while the Beam can.
questions.option_d: Polly doesn’t facilitate interaction between Henry and his friends whereas the Beam does.
questions.explanation: Both devices use similar components, but Polly is portable and therefore much smaller.

questions.question: In which space (A, B, C, or D) will this sentence fit? “He controls them using his head, and he's even flown one around his garden wearing a virtual reality headset.” Spaces: [A] before the Polly paragraph; [B] before the drone paragraph; [C] after the first sentence about flying drones; [D] after the sentence about the drone-video website.
questions.explanation: The pronouns them and one refer to drones introduced immediately before space C.

questions.question: Which of the following can be inferred about Henry from the last paragraph?
questions.option_a: He has already been approved to use a robot on the International Space Station.
questions.option_b: He has little hope of achieving his goal of exploring space remotely.
questions.option_c: He has shifted his focus from using drones to controlling robots in space.
questions.option_d: He is determined to keep exploring new possibilities despite his disability.
questions.explanation: He continues pursuing ambitious new ways to explore despite not yet receiving approval.

questions.question: Which sentence best summarizes the main idea of the passage?
questions.option_a: Henry Evans, at 52, uses advanced technology to help other disabled individuals experience the world in ways they couldn't before.
questions.option_b: Henry Evans, a disabled American, has explored space using innovative technologies like telepresence robots and drones.
questions.option_c: Henry Evans, a 52-year-old American, explores the world using telepresence robots and drones, aiming to one day travel to space.
questions.option_d: Henry Evans, an American inventor, designs telepresence robots and drones to enable disabled individuals to travel virtually.
questions.explanation: Option C accurately covers his virtual exploration and future aim without adding unsupported claims.

## PART 4 – Questions 21–25

Read the text and fill in **ONE word** which best fits each gap.

We know sleep is an activity we can’t do without, yet we let our hectic lifestyle wear us down until we can’t (21) ____ from bed in the morning. We know the longer we go without sleep, the more likely we are to have (22) ____ accident, and when that happens, this will be the unhappiest moment we’ve been through in our life. It’s safe to say that too many people have come up against this problem. But there’s no need for us to make ourselves tired over a lack of sleep. Now it seems as if people are bouncing back from this terrible (23) ____ torture by taking mid-day naps. Some may think it makes them look lazy to the boss, but these days aren’t as old-fashioned (24) ____ we might expect, and such ideas as napping at work are catching (25) ____. It’s been proven by researchers that a mid-day nap increases productivity, and more employees are changing their tune about the practice.
questions.explanation: 21 rise from bed; 22 have an accident; 23 sleep torture; 24 as ... as; 25 catch on.
